items: How ____ inventory space will the new shelving system free up?
Space is uncountable in this use, so 'much' is correct.
The training center can accommodate ____ participants in its largest room.
Participants are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The consultant spent ____ of the afternoon reviewing the compliance records.
Afternoon is a singular time period here and follows 'of the', so 'much of' is correct.
____ of the applications submitted online were missing a signature.
Applications are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
The revised schedule does not leave ____ time for additional testing.
Time is uncountable in this use, so 'much' is correct.
The loyalty program attracted ____ first-time shoppers during the campaign.
Shoppers are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The storm damaged ____ of the equipment stored near the loading dock.
Equipment is uncountable and follows 'of the', so 'much of' is correct.
How ____ of the regional managers will attend the strategy meeting in person?
Regional managers are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
The new packaging does not require ____ adhesive to keep the cartons sealed.
Adhesive is uncountable in this use, so 'much' is correct.
The recruiter interviewed ____ qualified applicants for the engineering vacancy.
Applicants are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The accounting team recovered ____ of the data from the corrupted backup.
Data is treated as uncountable here and follows 'of the', so 'much of' is correct.
____ of the conference rooms on the third floor have video equipment.
Conference rooms are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
There is not ____ room in the current budget for an unplanned advertising campaign.
Room meaning available capacity is uncountable here, so 'much' is correct.
The service center handles ____ warranty claims during the winter season.
Warranty claims are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The merger discussion occupied ____ of the board's meeting on Tuesday.
The meeting is a singular whole and follows 'of', so 'much of' is correct.
How ____ of the parcels scheduled for today have already left the warehouse?
Parcels are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
The interviewer did not receive ____ information about the candidate's previous role.
Information is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
The upgraded system allows ____ employees to work remotely at the same time.
Employees are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The renovation preserved ____ of the building's original character.
Character is uncountable in this sense and follows 'of', so 'much of' is correct.
____ of the suppliers on the approved list can deliver within two business days.
Suppliers are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
The audit found that the branch had not made ____ progress on the corrective plan.
Progress is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
The airport added ____ self-service kiosks near the international check-in area.
Kiosks are countable plural, so 'many' is correct.
The promotion generated ____ of the website traffic recorded last weekend.
Website traffic is uncountable and follows 'of the', so 'much of' is correct.
How ____ of the invoices in this folder still require a manager's approval?
Invoices are countable plural and follow 'of the', so 'many of' is correct.
The software does not use ____ bandwidth when running in offline mode.
Bandwidth is uncountable, so 'much' is correct.
